title: Infinity Policy v1
description: The rules the kernel applies. Only version and policy_id are required; the three lists default to empty. A policy can only RESTRICT, never grant: it can deny an effect or make it wait for a human. It cannot allow anything, and there is no allow-list. The kernel itself always denies the effects deploy, authority_change and audit_delete (FORBIDDEN_EFFECT) before it reads the policy, so with every list empty the only things that can ever be allowed are `read` and `write`. An empty policy is therefore not 'wide open': it is the least restrictive policy there is. As with proposals, the kernel is more lenient than this contract (it ignores unknown fields and denies a wrong version as UNKNOWN_POLICY_VERSION).

effects_requiring_approval.description: Effects that wait for a human (APPROVAL_REQUIRED).

risks_requiring_approval.description: Risk levels that wait for a human (APPROVAL_REQUIRED).
